name: Prompting techniques
desc: 553 prompting techniques from the Complete Catalog, grouped into 6 pillars, 19 families and related groups. Click any node to open it and read the details.

children.name: Instruction design
children.desc: How the request itself is written: wording, examples, roles and framing.

children.name: Foundations
children.desc: Every other technique sits on these basics: say clearly what you want, give the context, and separate instructions from data.

children.name: Zero-shot instruction
children.desc: Ask directly, with no examples. It is the baseline that every other technique changes.
children.origin: Radford et al., 2019; Brown et al., 2020

children.name: Clear, specific instructions
children.desc: State the task, its scope and the deliverable exactly. Write as if briefing a brilliant new hire who has no context.

children.name: Context provision
children.desc: Give the background, purpose, audience and situation that the model cannot infer.

children.name: Explain the why (motivation)
children.desc: Give the reason behind each rule so the model can apply it to cases you did not foresee.

children.name: Success criteria
children.desc: Say what a great answer looks like and how it will be judged.

children.name: Glossary and term definitions
children.desc: Define domain terms and labels so the model uses them consistently.

children.name: Exact quantities
children.desc: Use exact numbers, such as "3 bullets of up to 20 words", instead of "short".

children.name: Numbered sequential steps
children.desc: Break the instruction into ordered steps for the model to follow.

children.name: Delimiters
children.desc: Separate instructions from data with triple quotes, ### or code fences.

children.name: XML tagging
children.desc: Wrap each part in named tags, such as <document>, <instructions> and <example>, and refer to the tags by name.

children.name: Markdown structuring
children.desc: Split a long system prompt into sections with headings and bullets.

children.name: Prompt frameworks (mnemonics)
children.desc: Use a checklist such as CO-STAR, RTF, RISEN, CRISPE, RACE or CARE to cover context, objective, style, tone, audience and response.

children.name: Modular prompts
children.desc: Build prompts from reusable blocks (persona, policy, format) that are maintained separately.

children.name: Positive framing
children.desc: Say what to do rather than what not to do: "write in flowing prose", not "no markdown".

children.name: Explicit constraints
children.desc: Set hard limits: length, scope, exclusions, banned words and items that must be included.

children.name: Conditional (if–then) instructions
children.desc: Change behaviour based on properties of the input, for example "if the user asks about billing, …".

children.name: Edge-case and fallback instructions
children.desc: Say what to do with missing, ambiguous or out-of-scope input.

children.name: Permission to abstain
children.desc: Explicitly allow "I don't know" or "not enough information". This reduces hallucination.

children.name: Instruction priority ordering
children.desc: Say which rule wins when two rules conflict.

children.name: Removing ambiguity and conflict
children.desc: Remove vague or contradictory rules. Test: would a new colleague misread this?

children.name: Long-context ordering
children.desc: Put long documents at the top and the question at the end. This improves recall.
children.origin: Anthropic docs; Liu et al., 2023 (Lost in the Middle)

children.name: Instruction repetition (sandwich)
children.desc: Repeat the key instructions after a long input.

children.name: Emphasis markers
children.desc: Use IMPORTANT, capitals or bold to make a rule stand out. Use them sparingly, because newer models over-apply them.

children.name: System vs user placement
children.desc: Put stable identity and rules in the system prompt, and the task data in the user turn.

children.name: Prompt style matching
children.desc: Write the prompt in the style you want back: a prose prompt tends to get a prose answer.

children.name: Examples & ICL
children.desc: Showing beats telling: a few well-chosen demonstrations often fix format and quality faster than more instructions.

children.name: Few-shot prompting (one-shot to many-shot)
children.desc: Show the model one, a handful or hundreds of input-output demonstrations (in-context learning); long context windows make the many-shot end possible.
children.origin: Brown et al., 2020; Agarwal et al., 2024

children.name: Format-consistent demonstrations
children.desc: Make every example follow exactly the same structure and tags as the expected output.

children.name: Tagged examples
children.desc: Wrap examples in <example> tags so the model does not confuse them with instructions.

children.name: Example count tuning
children.desc: Treat the number of examples as a hyperparameter and measure. More is not always better.

children.name: Instruction plus examples
children.desc: Combine an explicit rule with examples. Each covers the other's gaps.

children.name: Multi-turn demonstrations
children.desc: Fake earlier user and assistant turns that show the desired behaviour.

children.name: Similarity-based exemplar selection (KATE)
children.desc: Retrieve the examples closest to the current input, for example by embedding search.

children.name: Diversity-based selection (Vote-k)
children.desc: Choose diverse, representative examples rather than near-duplicates.

children.name: Dynamic few-shot
children.desc: Assemble a fresh set of examples for every query from an example bank.

children.name: Active prompting
children.desc: Ask humans to annotate the questions the model is most uncertain about, then use those as exemplars.

children.name: Complexity-based exemplars
children.desc: Choose demonstrations with longer reasoning chains.

children.name: LENS (support-example search)
children.desc: Two-stage selection: filter for informative examples, then search for the best-performing set.

children.name: Learned demonstration retrievers (EPR, UDR)
children.desc: Train a retriever, scored by the model itself, to choose in-context examples, instead of using plain embedding similarity.
children.origin: Rubin et al., 2022; Li et al., 2023

children.name: Active example selection
children.desc: Use reinforcement learning to learn a policy that picks which demonstrations to include.

children.name: Exemplar ordering
children.desc: Order matters: test orderings, and put the most relevant example last.

children.name: Label balance and correctness
children.desc: Balance the class distribution. The format of the demonstrations often matters more than whether their labels are correct.

children.name: Contrastive (positive and negative) examples
children.desc: Show good and bad outputs, each labelled, so the model learns the boundary.

children.name: Explanations in demonstrations
children.desc: Attach a short rationale to each example.

children.name: Counterfactual demonstrations
children.desc: Examples that vary one factor, to teach which feature actually matters.

children.name: Ambiguous demonstrations
children.desc: Choose exemplars whose labels fall in the model's confusable label set for the test input.

children.name: AlignedCoT (native-style demonstrations)
children.desc: Rewrite CoT demonstrations in the model's own zero-shot reasoning style instead of human-written style.

children.name: Self-generated ICL (SG-ICL)
children.desc: The model writes its own demonstrations when no labelled data exists.

children.name: Auto-CoT exemplars
children.desc: Cluster the questions, then let the model write reasoning demonstrations for a representative of each cluster.

children.name: Self-Instruct
children.desc: Grow a set of instructions from a few seeds: the model writes new tasks, inputs and outputs, which are then filtered (synthetic data).

children.name: Evol-Instruct
children.desc: Rewrite instructions repeatedly to make them more complex (in-depth) or more diverse (in-breadth).

children.name: AttrPrompt
children.desc: Generate synthetic data from prompts that vary set attributes (length, style, topic), so the data is diverse and less biased.

children.name: LEAP (principles learned from mistakes)
children.desc: Let the model fail on the few-shot examples, reflect to write task-specific principles, then add those principles to the prompt.

children.name: Role & framing
children.desc: Who the model is, who it is talking to, and how the situation is framed all change tone, depth and which knowledge it brings forward.

children.name: Role (persona) prompting
children.desc: "You are a senior tax accountant…" sets the domain, vocabulary and standards.

children.name: ExpertPrompting
children.desc: The model first writes a detailed expert identity for the question, then answers in that identity.

children.name: Audience persona
children.desc: Specify the reader: "explain to a 10-year-old", "for a board of directors".

children.name: Character role-play
children.desc: Sustained in-character dialogue for fiction, games and training simulations.

children.name: Teacher or Socratic tutor role
children.desc: The model guides with questions and does not hand over answers.

children.name: Role-play prompting (two-stage immersion)
children.desc: First establish the role in its own turn and let the model accept it, then ask the question. This improves zero-shot reasoning.

children.name: Solo Performance Prompting (multi-persona)
children.desc: One model simulates several experts who work together on the task.

children.name: Jekyll & Hyde ensembling
children.desc: Answer with and without a persona, then let a judge pick the better answer.

children.name: Simulated stakeholder or user
children.desc: The model plays a customer, interviewer, patient or opponent for practice or testing.

children.name: Critic or devil's advocate persona
children.desc: Ask the model to attack an idea or argue the opposite side.

children.name: Steelmanning
children.desc: Ask for the strongest version of a position before evaluating it.

children.name: Perspective-taking (SimToM)
children.desc: Filter the context down to what one character knows before answering theory-of-mind questions.

children.name: Hypothetical framing
children.desc: "Suppose that…" or "in a world where…" to explore scenarios.

children.name: Counterfactual prompting
children.desc: Ask what would change if one fact were different, to test causal understanding.

children.name: Neutral framing (anti-sycophancy)
children.desc: Hide your own preference, or present your draft as someone else's, so the model does not just agree.

children.name: Premise checking
children.desc: Tell the model to verify the question's assumptions before answering.

children.name: Stakes and situation framing
children.desc: Describe the real use and its consequences, such as "this goes into a legal filing".

children.name: Debiasing instruction
children.desc: Tell the model directly to treat groups equally and not rely on stereotypes.

children.name: System prompt as constitution
children.desc: A standing charter of values, identity and boundaries for every turn.

children.name: Identity anchoring
children.desc: Give the assistant a stable name, voice and boundaries so it stays consistent across long conversations.

children.name: Persistent user profile
children.desc: Custom instructions or memory that tell the model who you are and how you like answers, applied to every chat.

children.name: Stimulus & folk
children.desc: These phrasing tricks circulate widely. The evidence for them is mixed and often model-specific, so treat them as things to test, not rules.

children.name: EmotionPrompt
children.desc: Add emotional stakes, such as "This is very important to my career."
children.origin: Li et al., 2023: gains on older models; weaker on newer ones

children.name: "Take a deep breath" phrasing
children.desc: A calming preamble that an optimiser discovered for PaLM 2.

children.name: Politeness
children.desc: Saying please and thank you.
children.origin: Yin et al., 2024: rude prompts hurt; excess politeness doesn't help

children.name: Flattery of the model's expertise
children.desc: "You are the world's best…"
children.origin: Zheng et al., 2023: little factual gain

children.name: Tipping or incentive offers
children.desc: "I'll tip $200 for a perfect answer."
children.origin: Bsharat et al., 2023: small and inconsistent effects

children.name: Threats or penalties
children.desc: "You will be penalised if…"
children.origin: Bsharat et al., 2023: unreliable; not recommended

children.name: Deadline or urgency framing
children.desc: "I need this in 5 minutes."

children.name: "Unlimited time" framing
children.desc: "Take as long as you need; quality over speed."

children.name: Principled-instructions checklist
children.desc: 26 rules, such as "use affirmative directives" and "you MUST".

children.name: Repetition of key words
children.desc: Repeat the core instruction several times.

children.name: Reasoning & verification
children.desc: Making the model think, break problems down, check itself and combine answers.

children.name: Reasoning
children.desc: Making the model reason before it answers is the most studied family. On today's reasoning models, built-in thinking replaces much of the manual chain-of-thought.

children.name: Chain-of-Thought (few-shot CoT)
children.desc: Demonstrations include step-by-step reasoning before the answer.

children.name: Zero-shot CoT
children.desc: Add "Let's think step by step."

children.name: Structured thinking tags
children.desc: Reason inside <thinking> and answer inside <answer>, so the reasoning can be parsed out or hidden.

children.name: Extended thinking / reasoning budget
children.desc: Turn on the model's native thinking mode and set its budget or effort level. Give high-level guidance rather than step-by-step scripts.

children.name: Interleaved thinking
children.desc: Let the model reason between tool calls, not only before the first answer.

children.name: Chain of Draft
children.desc: CoT with very short draft notes per step, to save tokens.

children.name: Think-then-answer separation
children.desc: Make the model commit to reasoning before the verdict, never the verdict first.

children.name: Scratchpad
children.desc: Have the model write intermediate computations to a scratchpad before the final output. A forerunner of CoT.

children.name: Self-Harmonized CoT (ECHO)
children.desc: Refine auto-generated CoT demonstrations so they converge on one consistent reasoning pattern.

children.name: Instance-adaptive zero-shot CoT (IAP)
children.desc: Pick the best zero-shot CoT trigger phrase for each question separately, rather than one fixed phrase.

children.name: Thinking Intervention
children.desc: Insert or revise guidance tokens directly inside a reasoning model's thinking, to steer how it follows instructions and safety rules.

children.name: Tree of Thoughts
children.desc: Branch into several partial solutions, evaluate them and search (BFS or DFS), with backtracking.

children.name: Graph of Thoughts
children.desc: Thoughts form a graph that can merge, refine and loop.

children.name: Algorithm of Thoughts
children.desc: Show algorithmic search paths inside one prompt to get ToT-like exploration in a single call.

children.name: Everything of Thoughts (XoT)
children.desc: Use MCTS with small models to guide the thought search.

children.name: Cumulative Reasoning
children.desc: Proposer, verifier and reporter roles build a growing set of verified facts.

children.name: Recursion of Thought
children.desc: Hand sub-problems to new context windows recursively to get past length limits.

children.name: Thought Propagation
children.desc: Solve analogous problems and transfer their solutions.

children.name: Reasoning via Planning (RAP)
children.desc: Use the model as a world model and plan with MCTS.

children.name: Tree of Uncertain Thought
children.desc: Add uncertainty estimates to the nodes of a ToT search.

children.name: Single-prompt Tree-of-Thought
children.desc: "Imagine three experts answering; each writes one step, shares it, and any who are wrong drop out." This gives ToT in one call.

children.name: Program of Thoughts
children.desc: Reason by writing code, and let an interpreter do the computation.

children.name: Program-Aided Language models (PAL)
children.desc: Turn the problem into a program and run it.

children.name: Chain of Code
children.desc: Write code, and let the model "emulate" lines that cannot actually run.

children.name: Faithful CoT
children.desc: Translate into a symbolic form (code, PDDL, Datalog) and solve deterministically.

children.name: Tabular CoT (Tab-CoT)
children.desc: Reason in a markdown table, one row per step.

children.name: Chain of Symbol
children.desc: Use compact symbols instead of language for spatial reasoning.

children.name: Chain-of-Table
children.desc: Reason over tables by planning and applying table operations step by step.

children.name: Binder
children.desc: Parse the question into a program (SQL or Python) that can call the LLM as a function for the parts code can't handle.

children.name: Code prompting (NL-to-code reformulation)
children.desc: Rewrite a natural-language reasoning problem as code (variables, if-blocks) and have the model reason over that code.

children.name: Structured-data serialization
children.desc: Choose how a table or graph is encoded as text (markdown, JSON, HTML, edge lists), because the encoding changes accuracy a lot.
children.origin: Sui et al., 2024; Fatemi et al., 2023

children.name: Logical CoT (LogiCoT)
children.desc: Check each step with symbolic-logic principles such as reductio ad absurdum.

children.name: Maieutic prompting
children.desc: Build a tree of abductive explanations and resolve their consistency logically.

children.name: Selection-Inference
children.desc: Alternate between selecting the relevant facts and drawing one inference from them.

children.name: Natural Program (deductive verification)
children.desc: Reasoning steps in a structured format, each citing its premises so it can be checked.

children.name: Process of Elimination (POE)
children.desc: Score and eliminate the wrong multiple-choice options first, then choose from the ones left.

children.name: Logic-of-Thought (LoT)
children.desc: Extract propositions, expand them with logical laws (contraposition, transitivity), and add the results back to the prompt.

children.name: EEDP (End-to-End DAG-Path) prompting
children.desc: Flatten a graph into text around its main backbone paths, so the model can reason over long-range dependencies.

children.name: Chain of Logic
children.desc: Rule-based reasoning: split a rule into elements, resolve each one, then recombine them through the rule's logical expression.

children.name: Hypotheses-to-Theories (HtT)
children.desc: Induce rules from training examples, keep the verified ones, and put that rule library in the prompt for later deduction.

children.name: Thread of Thought
children.desc: "Walk me through this context in manageable parts step by step, summarizing and analyzing as we go." Built for chaotic contexts.

children.name: Self-Ask
children.desc: The model asks itself explicit follow-up questions, answers them, then answers the main question.

children.name: System 2 Attention (S2A)
children.desc: First rewrite the context to remove irrelevant or biasing text, then answer.

children.name: Rephrase and Respond (RaR)
children.desc: The model rephrases and expands the question, then answers it.

children.name: Re-reading (RE2)
children.desc: Repeat the question: "Read the question again: …".

children.name: EchoPrompt
children.desc: The model restates the query before answering.

children.name: Self-Polish
children.desc: The model refines a badly worded problem into a clearer one before solving it.

children.name: Step-back prompting
children.desc: Ask first for the general principle or concept behind the question, then answer.

children.name: Analogical prompting
children.desc: The model recalls related solved problems before solving the target.

children.name: Memory-of-Thought
children.desc: Pre-think on unlabelled data and save good thoughts to recall at test time.

children.name: Buffer of Thoughts
children.desc: Keep a library of reusable thought templates and instantiate the right one.

children.name: Self-Discover
children.desc: The model picks and adapts reasoning modules ("critical thinking", "step by step") into a task-specific plan.

children.name: Meta-CoT
children.desc: Classify the type of question first, then choose the CoT demonstrations to match.

children.name: Mental-model frameworks
children.desc: Ask for reasoning through a named lens: first principles, six thinking hats, SWOT, inversion or second-order effects.

children.name: Metacognitive Prompting
children.desc: Five stages: understand the input, make a first judgment, evaluate it critically, decide with an explanation, and assess confidence.

children.name: Skeleton-of-Thought
children.desc: Write an outline first, then expand the points in parallel for speed.

children.name: Contrastive CoT
children.desc: Show both valid and invalid reasoning chains.

children.name: Progressive-Hint Prompting
children.desc: Feed earlier answers back in as hints until the answer is stable.

children.name: Directional Stimulus Prompting
children.desc: A small policy model generates hint keywords that steer the main model.

children.name: Uncertainty-routed CoT
children.desc: Sample several CoTs and take the majority answer if agreement passes a threshold; otherwise use the greedy answer.

children.name: Hint or partial-solution priming
children.desc: Give the first step, or a key insight, and let the model finish.

children.name: Worked-example scaffolding
children.desc: Show one fully solved problem, then pose a similar one.

children.name: Contrastive prompting
children.desc: Zero-shot trigger: "Let's give a correct and a wrong answer", so the model separates the two.

children.name: Clue And Reasoning Prompting (CARP)
children.desc: For classification: list surface clues, reason over them, then decide on the label.

children.name: Narrative-of-Thought (NoT)
children.desc: For temporal reasoning: turn the events into a Python structure and have the model retell them as a time-ordered story.

children.name: IRAC legal reasoning
children.desc: Structure legal analysis as Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion, through demonstrations or a fixed scaffold.

children.name: Diagnostic reasoning prompts
children.desc: Clinical CoT that follows how clinicians reason (differential, analytic, Bayesian, intuitive), so diagnoses are interpretable.

children.name: Decomposition & chaining
children.desc: Splitting a hard task into smaller prompts or sub-questions makes each step easier, and each step can be checked on its own.

children.name: Least-to-Most
children.desc: Break the task into sub-problems from easiest to hardest and solve them in order, feeding answers forward.

children.name: Decomposed Prompting (DecomP)
children.desc: Hand sub-tasks to specialised sub-prompts or tools.

children.name: Plan-and-Solve (PS, PS+)
children.desc: "First devise a plan, then carry it out step by step."

children.name: Successive Prompting
children.desc: Ask and answer simpler questions one at a time, in a loop.

children.name: Factored question decomposition
children.desc: Answer each sub-question in a separate context so they cannot contaminate each other.

children.name: Socratic Questioning
children.desc: Recursively ask and answer sub-questions, top-down, until confident.

children.name: Prompt chaining (AI Chains)
children.desc: The output of one prompt becomes the input of the next, in a fixed pipeline.

children.name: Outline-then-expand
children.desc: Generate the structure, approve it, then write each part.

children.name: Plan-and-Execute
children.desc: A planner writes the whole plan up front, and an executor runs it step by step.

children.name: Routing
children.desc: Classify the input first, then send it to a specialised prompt or model.

children.name: Parallelization (sectioning)
children.desc: Run independent sub-tasks at the same time and merge them.

children.name: Gate checks between steps
children.desc: Validate each intermediate output in code before the chain continues.

children.name: LLM+P (planner hand-off)
children.desc: Translate the planning problem into PDDL, solve it with a classical planner, and translate the plan back.

children.name: Map-reduce
children.desc: Process chunks independently (map), then combine the results (reduce).

children.name: Hierarchical (recursive) prompting
children.desc: A parent prompt plans and child prompts carry out the parts, recursively.

children.name: Divide and conquer for long inputs
children.desc: Split long documents, process each part, then combine with a final prompt.

children.name: Batch prompting
children.desc: Put several inputs in one prompt and answer them all in one call, to cut cost and latency.

children.name: ChatIE (multi-turn extraction)
children.desc: Zero-shot extraction as a chat: ask which element types are present, then extract each type's slots in follow-up turns.

children.name: Self-critique & ensembles
children.desc: Asking the model to check, critique or vote across several attempts catches errors that a single pass misses.

children.name: Self-Refine
children.desc: Generate, critique your own output, revise, and repeat.

children.name: Recursive Criticism and Improvement (RCI)
children.desc: "Review your previous answer and find problems with it", then improve it.

children.name: Constitutional critique and revision
children.desc: Critique the output against written principles, then rewrite it.

children.name: Pre-mortem
children.desc: "Assume this plan failed; explain why." This surfaces hidden risks.

children.name: "Are you sure?" re-check
children.desc: A second-pass review prompt. Beware: models may flip a correct answer under pressure.

children.name: Red-team your own answer
children.desc: Ask the model to attack its answer as a hostile reviewer would.

children.name: Chain-of-Verification (CoVe)
children.desc: Draft an answer, plan verification questions, answer them independently, then revise.

children.name: Self-Verification
children.desc: Check a candidate answer by working backwards from it to the conditions.

children.name: Reversing CoT (RCoT)
children.desc: Rebuild the problem from the answer and compare it with the original to find overlooked conditions.

children.name: CRITIC
children.desc: Verify claims with external tools (search, code) and correct them.

children.name: Verify-and-Edit
children.desc: Edit reasoning chains using retrieved facts.

children.name: RARR
children.desc: Research and revise a draft afterwards to add attribution and fix unsupported claims.

children.name: Fact-check list
children.desc: List the factual claims the answer depends on so they can be checked.

children.name: SelfCheckGPT
children.desc: Sample several responses and treat disagreement between them as a sign that a claim is hallucinated.

children.name: LM vs LM cross-examination
children.desc: An examiner model questions the examinee over several turns to expose inconsistencies that reveal factual errors.

children.name: Self-contradiction detection
children.desc: Generate alternative sentences in the same context, find statements that contradict each other, and remove or revise them.

children.name: Self-calibration (P(True))
children.desc: Ask the model whether its own answer is true and read the confidence.

children.name: Verbalized confidence
children.desc: Ask for a confidence score or level with each claim.

children.name: Max Mutual Information
children.desc: Pick the template that maximises mutual information between prompt and output.

children.name: Semantic entropy
children.desc: Sample several answers, group them by meaning (bidirectional entailment), and use the entropy across the groups to detect confabulation.
children.origin: Kuhn et al., 2023; Farquhar et al., 2024

children.name: Self-consistency
children.desc: Sample several reasoning paths and take the majority answer.

children.name: Universal Self-Consistency
children.desc: Let the model itself pick the most consistent free-form answer.

children.name: DiVeRSe
children.desc: Use diverse prompts plus a trained verifier that scores each step.

children.name: Multi-Chain Reasoning (MCR)
children.desc: A meta-reasoner reads several chains and combines their evidence.

children.name: COSP / USP
children.desc: Self-consistency picks confident outputs to reuse as zero-shot exemplars.

children.name: Self-evaluation guided beam search
children.desc: The model scores each reasoning step for correctness, and those scores steer a step-level beam search.

children.name: Choice shuffling
children.desc: Permute the multiple-choice options across runs and vote, to cancel position bias.
children.origin: Nori et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2023 (PriDe)

children.name: Medprompt
children.desc: A composite recipe: kNN few-shot examples, self-generated CoT and a choice-shuffle ensemble. A generalist model matched specialist medical models with it.

children.name: Demonstration Ensembling (DENSE)
children.desc: Run separate few-shot prompts with different exemplar subsets and aggregate.

children.name: Mixture of Reasoning Experts (MoRE)
children.desc: Use specialised prompts per reasoning type and select by agreement.

children.name: Prompt paraphrasing ensembles
children.desc: Ask the same question in several wordings and aggregate.

children.name: Boosted prompting
children.desc: Add exemplars for the hard examples where the current ensemble fails.

children.name: Ask Me Anything (AMA)
children.desc: Reformat the task into several open-ended QA prompts and combine their noisy answers with weak supervision.

children.name: Multi-agent debate
children.desc: Several model instances argue and converge on an answer.
children.origin: Du et al., 2023; Liang et al., 2023

children.name: Mixture-of-Agents
children.desc: Layers of models refine and aggregate each other's outputs.

children.name: LLM-Blender
children.desc: Rank candidates pairwise, then fuse the best ones.

children.name: Best-of-N with a judge
children.desc: Generate N candidates and let a grader prompt choose.

children.name: Knowledge, tools & agents
children.desc: Grounding answers in sources and letting the model act through tools and agents.

children.name: Retrieval & grounding
children.desc: Grounding answers in supplied or retrieved text is the main defence against hallucination.

children.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
children.desc: Retrieve relevant passages and put them in the prompt.

children.name: Contextual retrieval
children.desc: Prepend a short, model-written context line to each chunk before indexing it.

children.name: LLM re-ranking (RankGPT)
children.desc: Prompt the model to rank the retrieved passages by relevance.

children.name: Small-to-big (parent document) retrieval
children.desc: Match on small chunks, but give the model the larger parent section.

children.name: Long-context stuffing
children.desc: Skip retrieval and put the whole corpus in a large context window.

children.name: Document metadata tagging
children.desc: Wrap each document with source, date and title tags so it can be cited and filtered.

children.name: Self-querying retrieval
children.desc: The model turns a query into a semantic search string plus structured metadata filters (date, author, type).

children.name: Attention sorting
children.desc: Decode once, reorder the documents by how much attention they got (most-attended last), then answer again. This counters recency bias.

children.name: Closed-context restriction
children.desc: "Answer only from the documents provided; otherwise say you can't."

children.name: Quote-first grounding
children.desc: Extract the relevant quotes into tags first, then answer using only those quotes.

children.name: Required citations
children.desc: Tie each claim to a source ID or passage, in a set format.

children.name: Line or passage numbering
children.desc: Number the sentences or paragraphs of the source so the model can cite them exactly and you can verify them.

children.name: "According to…" prompting
children.desc: Tell the model to ground its answer in a named source ("According to Wikipedia…"). This raises quoting of real pre-training text.

children.name: FreshPrompt
children.desc: Insert dated search results in chronological order, with demonstrations, for time-sensitive questions.

children.name: Context-faithful prompting
children.desc: Frame the context as a quoted statement ("Bob said…") and/or add counterfactual demonstrations, so the model follows the context over its memory.

children.name: HyDE
children.desc: Generate a hypothetical answer and use its embedding to retrieve real documents.

children.name: Query rewriting (Rewrite-Retrieve-Read)
children.desc: Rewrite the user query into a better search query before retrieving.

children.name: Multi-query / RAG-Fusion
children.desc: Generate several query variants and fuse the ranked results.

children.name: Step-back retrieval
children.desc: Retrieve for the more general step-back question as well as the specific one.

children.name: Self-RAG
children.desc: The model decides when to retrieve and critiques relevance and support with reflection tokens.

children.name: Corrective RAG (CRAG)
children.desc: Grade the retrieved documents; if they are poor, fall back to web search or refine the query.

children.name: FLARE (active retrieval)
children.desc: Retrieve again whenever upcoming tokens look low-confidence.

children.name: IRCoT
children.desc: Interleave retrieval with each chain-of-thought step.

children.name: Demonstrate-Search-Predict (DSP)
children.desc: A composable pipeline of demonstrations, search and prediction.

children.name: Chain-of-Note
children.desc: Write reading notes on each retrieved document to judge its relevance before answering.

children.name: Generated knowledge prompting
children.desc: The model first writes relevant facts, then answers using them.

children.name: Recitation-augmented generation
children.desc: Recite relevant passages from memory before answering.

children.name: Chain-of-Knowledge
children.desc: Ground reasoning steps in knowledge sources, adapted step by step.

children.name: Imitate, Retrieve, Paraphrase (IRP)
children.desc: For expository writing: plan like a style exemplar, retrieve the facts, then paraphrase them into that style.

children.name: In-context knowledge editing (IKE)
children.desc: Override or update a fact with no weight changes, using demonstrations of copying, updating and keeping facts.

children.name: Knowledge-graph prompting (Think-on-Graph)
children.desc: Explore a knowledge graph step by step during reasoning.

children.name: GraphRAG
children.desc: Build an entity graph and community summaries for answering global questions.

children.name: RAPTOR
children.desc: Retrieve over a tree of recursive summaries.

children.name: ReadAgent (gist memory)
children.desc: Page a long text, compress each page into a gist, and let the model look up the original pages it needs when answering.

children.name: MemWalker
children.desc: Build a tree of summaries over a long text and let the model navigate it, choosing which branches to read.

children.name: Retrieval-augmented personalisation (LaMP)
children.desc: Retrieve the user's own past items (posts, ratings, emails) into the prompt so the output fits that user.

children.name: Recommendation prompting (recency-focused)
children.desc: Present the interaction history in order, stress the most recent items, and ask the model to rank the candidates.

children.name: Tools & agents
children.desc: Once a model acts in loops with tools, prompting becomes context engineering: deciding what goes into the window at each step.

children.name: Function / tool calling
children.desc: Describe tools with schemas, and let the model emit structured calls.

children.name: Tool descriptions as prompts
children.desc: Write tool names, descriptions and parameter docs as carefully as the main prompt.

children.name: "Think" tool
children.desc: A no-op tool that gives the agent a place to reason between tool calls.

children.name: Agent-computer interface design
children.desc: Design tool outputs and commands for the model (concise, with clear errors).

children.name: Parallel tool-call instruction
children.desc: Tell the model to batch independent tool calls in one turn.

children.name: Tool-use examples
children.desc: Attach concrete example calls to a tool's definition, showing correct parameter use beyond what the schema says.

children.name: CodeAct / programmatic tool calling
children.desc: The agent acts by writing code that calls tools, loops and composes results, instead of making one JSON call at a time.

children.name: Tool search (dynamic tool retrieval)
children.desc: Keep a large tool library out of the context and let the model search for and load tool definitions on demand.

children.name: Tool preambles
children.desc: Before calling tools, the agent restates the goal and outlines its plan, then narrates progress as it works.

children.name: ReAct
children.desc: Interleave Thought, Action and Observation in a loop.

children.name: MRKL
children.desc: A router sends sub-queries to expert modules and tools.

children.name: Toolformer-style self-annotation
children.desc: The model learns where to insert API calls in its text.

children.name: ART
children.desc: Retrieve multi-step reasoning and tool-use demonstrations from a task library.

children.name: Chameleon / HuggingGPT
children.desc: An LLM planner composes calls to many tools or models.
children.origin: Lu et al., 2023; Shen et al., 2023

children.name: ReWOO
children.desc: Plan all tool calls up front with variable placeholders, then run them without stopping to observe.

children.name: LLMCompiler
children.desc: Plan a DAG of tool calls and run independent ones in parallel.

children.name: Tool-Integrated Reasoning (ToRA)
children.desc: Interleave natural-language reasoning with program execution and feed the results back to the model.

children.name: TaskWeaver
children.desc: A code-first agent framework: user requests become executable code, and plugins are callable functions.

children.name: Reflexion
children.desc: Verbal self-reflection after a failure is stored in memory for the next attempt.

children.name: Language Agent Tree Search (LATS)
children.desc: MCTS over agent actions, with reflection and value estimates.

children.name: Voyager skill library
children.desc: Store working code skills and retrieve them for new tasks.

children.name: Agentic Context Engineering (evolving playbooks)
children.desc: Generator, reflector and curator roles update a strategy playbook in the context in small increments, so knowledge is not lost when the context is rewritten.
children.origin: Zhang et al., 2025; Suzgun et al., 2025 (Dynamic Cheatsheet)

children.name: Ghost in the Minecraft (GITM)
children.desc: Break goals down recursively into sub-goals and structured actions, with text knowledge and memory.

children.name: Ralph loop
children.desc: Re-run the same prompt to a coding agent over and over in a fresh context, with progress kept in files and git, until the task is done.

children.name: Role-playing agent societies (CAMEL)
children.desc: Two agents in user and assistant roles work together through inception prompts.

children.name: Multi-agent conversation (AutoGen)
children.desc: Conversable agents with defined roles talk to each other to solve a task.

children.name: SOP-encoded agents (MetaGPT, ChatDev)
children.desc: Standard operating procedures and company roles are written into the agents' prompts.
children.origin: Hong et al., 2023; Qian et al., 2023

children.name: Orchestrator-workers
children.desc: A lead model splits the work up on the fly and hands it to sub-agents.

children.name: Evaluator-optimizer loop
children.desc: One prompt generates and another evaluates, until the evaluator is satisfied.

children.name: Parallel voting
children.desc: Run the same task several times and combine the results for confidence.

children.name: Sub-agent context isolation
children.desc: Give sub-agents clean contexts and return only condensed results.

children.name: Generative-agent memory and reflection
children.desc: A memory stream with retrieval by recency, importance and relevance, plus periodic reflection.

children.name: MemGPT (virtual context)
children.desc: The agent pages information between its context and external memory.

children.name: Compaction
children.desc: Summarise the conversation and restart with the summary when the context fills up.

children.name: Structured note-taking
children.desc: The agent keeps a NOTES.md, a to-do list or progress files outside the context window.

children.name: Just-in-time context
children.desc: Keep references (paths, IDs) and load the content only when it is needed.

children.name: Progressive disclosure (skills)
children.desc: Show short skill descriptions first and load the full instructions only when relevant.

children.name: Tool-result clearing
children.desc: Remove stale tool outputs from the history.

children.name: Project memory files
children.desc: Persistent instruction files such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, loaded into every session.

children.name: Recursive Language Models (RLM)
children.desc: The long context lives as a variable in a REPL; the model writes code to inspect and split it, and calls itself recursively on the pieces.

children.name: Stop conditions and iteration caps
children.desc: Explicit criteria for when the agent finishes or hands back to the user.

children.name: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
children.desc: Tell the agent to pause for approval before irreversible actions.

children.name: Error-recovery instructions
children.desc: Say how to react to tool errors: retry, fall back or report.

children.name: Agentic eagerness calibration
children.desc: Set how proactive the agent is: act or only suggest, how much to explore, tool-call budgets, and persistence until the task is done.

children.name: Code as Policies
children.desc: Few-shot prompts that have the model write robot-control code calling perception and control APIs.

children.name: Inner Monologue
children.desc: Feed environment feedback (success detection, scene descriptions) back into an embodied agent's prompt as closed-loop text.

children.name: SayCan
children.desc: Rank the skills the model proposes by combining its scores with value functions that say what the robot can actually do.

children.name: Output & conversation
children.desc: Controlling what comes back and how the exchange with the model unfolds.

children.name: Output control
children.desc: Shape the output so that people can read it and code can parse it reliably, then extract the answer robustly.

children.name: Output format specification
children.desc: Name the exact format: JSON, a table, bullets, sections, a markdown or plain-text style.

children.name: Schema-in-prompt
children.desc: Paste the JSON schema or TypeScript type that the output must follow.

children.name: Structured outputs / JSON mode
children.desc: Use API-level constrained decoding to a schema.

children.name: Grammar-constrained decoding
children.desc: Use a CFG or regex to restrict the tokens the model can produce.

children.name: Response prefilling
children.desc: Write the opening of the assistant's reply, such as { or <answer>, to lock the format or skip a preamble.

children.name: Output template
children.desc: Give a fill-in-the-blanks skeleton of the answer.

children.name: Section tags for parsing
children.desc: Ask for the answer inside <answer> and the reasoning inside <reasoning>, so code can extract them.

children.name: Stop sequences
children.desc: Stop generation at a delimiter to cut off rambling.

children.name: Ordered output fields
children.desc: Put the reasoning fields before the verdict fields in a schema, so the model reasons first.

children.name: Answer-space restriction
children.desc: Limit the answer to a fixed set: "answer only with A, B, C or D".

children.name: Verbalizer design
children.desc: Map labels to the words the model is most likely to say, such as "positive"/"negative" rather than 1/0.

children.name: Answer extraction
children.desc: Pull the answer out with a regex, a separator token or a second extractor prompt.

children.name: Noisy channel prompting
children.desc: Score P(input | label) instead of P(label | input). This is more stable with imbalanced or very few demonstrations.

children.name: Domain-conditional PMI scoring
children.desc: Rank answer options by PMI against a domain premise, to fix surface-form competition between equivalent answers.

children.name: Inline entity marking (GPT-NER)
children.desc: Rewrite the input with entities wrapped in markers (@@…##), then self-verify each entity.

children.name: Codebook prompting
children.desc: For annotation and labelling, give the full codebook: label definitions, inclusion and exclusion rules, and borderline examples.

children.name: Length control
children.desc: Set word or sentence counts, a number of bullets, or "one line".

children.name: Uncertainty reporting
children.desc: Ask for confidence levels or a "what I'm unsure about" section.

children.name: Tone and style specification
children.desc: Name the register, voice and reading level.

children.name: Formatting-avoidance steering
children.desc: To get less markdown, write the prompt in prose and ask for flowing paragraphs.

children.name: Audience-calibrated detail
children.desc: Set the depth for the reader: an expert summary versus a beginner's walkthrough.

children.name: Tail generation
children.desc: End every reply with a set footer, such as next steps or a question back.

children.name: Output automater
children.desc: Ask the model to output a script that carries out its own recommended steps.

children.name: Visualization generator
children.desc: Ask for the output as Graphviz, Mermaid or plotting code.

children.name: Interaction patterns
children.desc: These patterns shape how a multi-turn conversation unfolds, and many come from White et al.'s Prompt Pattern Catalog.

children.name: Flipped interaction
children.desc: The model asks you questions until it has what it needs, then acts.

children.name: Clarify-first
children.desc: "Before answering, ask me up to 3 clarifying questions."

children.name: Question refinement
children.desc: The model suggests a better version of your question.

children.name: Cognitive verifier
children.desc: The model splits your question into sub-questions, collects your answers, then combines them.

children.name: Interview-me
children.desc: The model interviews you to draw out requirements or your knowledge.

children.name: Proactive CoT (ProCoT)
children.desc: Before each reply, plan the dialogue strategy (clarify, steer toward a target, negotiate), then respond.

children.name: Alternative approaches
children.desc: Ask for several different ways to do the task, with trade-offs.

children.name: Reflection pattern
children.desc: The model explains the reasoning and assumptions behind its answer.

children.name: Refusal explanation (Refusal Breaker)
children.desc: When it can't answer, the model explains why and suggests a rewording it can answer.

children.name: Iterative refinement
children.desc: Improve the output over several turns with targeted feedback.

children.name: Edit-in-place feedback
children.desc: Quote the exact part to change and say what to do with it.

children.name: Context manager
children.desc: Tell the model what to keep in focus or ignore: "ignore the earlier draft".

children.name: Semantic filter
children.desc: Have the model filter information, such as removing personal data or keeping only budget items.

children.name: Multi-turn scaffolding
children.desc: Build up the context across turns before the main request.

children.name: Summarise-and-continue
children.desc: Summarise the conversation so far and carry it into a fresh chat.

children.name: Fresh-context reset
children.desc: Start a new chat to escape a polluted or anchored context.

children.name: "Continue" prompting
children.desc: Ask the model to continue a truncated output exactly where it stopped.

children.name: Cue-CoT
children.desc: In dialogue, first infer the user's state (personality, emotion, needs) from cues, then reply to fit it.

children.name: Teach-back
children.desc: The model checks your understanding by asking you to explain it back.

children.name: Role reversal
children.desc: You play the expert and the model plays the learner or critic.

children.name: Rubber-duck prompting
children.desc: Explain your problem to the model; it listens and asks probing questions.

children.name: Meta language creation
children.desc: Define a shorthand, such as "a → b means…", that the model then understands.

children.name: Recipe
children.desc: Give partial steps and let the model complete and order the full sequence.

children.name: Infinite generation
children.desc: Keep producing outputs, such as variants, until you say stop.

children.name: Game play
children.desc: The model runs a game or simulation with rules you define.

children.name: System emulation
children.desc: "Act as a Linux terminal, SQL database or REST API; reply only with what it would output." Useful for mocking and teaching.

children.name: Domains & modalities
children.desc: Techniques specific to writing, code, other languages, images, audio and video.

children.name: Writing & summaries
children.desc: Writing tasks gain most from voice samples, constraints and draft–critique–revise loops. Summaries gain from controlling density and structure.

children.name: Voice from samples
children.desc: Paste samples of the target voice and ask the model to match them.

children.name: Style transfer
children.desc: Rewrite the content in a different register, genre or author-like style.

children.name: Show-don't-tell exemplars
children.desc: Give passages showing the effect you want instead of describing it.

children.name: Anti-cliché lists
children.desc: Ban the overused phrases and structures typical of model writing.

children.name: Reading-level targeting
children.desc: Set a grade level or Flesch score, or "explain like I'm 5".

children.name: Persuasion frameworks
children.desc: Ask for a set structure, such as AIDA, PAS or SCQA.

children.name: Constraint writing
children.desc: Formal constraints (word limits, a rhyme scheme, banned letters) force fresh output.

children.name: Divergent then convergent
children.desc: Brainstorm many options, then choose and develop the best.

children.name: Perspective shifting
children.desc: Retell or argue from several viewpoints.

children.name: Story bible / canon document
children.desc: Characters, world rules and timeline kept in context for consistency.

children.name: Randomness injection
children.desc: Add random seed words, constraints or personas to escape generic output.

children.name: Verbalized sampling
children.desc: Ask for several responses with their probabilities, to counter mode collapse and add diversity.

children.name: Draft → critique → revise
children.desc: Write, critique against a rubric, then rewrite.

children.name: Editing passes
children.desc: Run separate prompts for structure, clarity, concision and copy-editing.

children.name: Re3 (Recursive Reprompting and Revision)
children.desc: Long stories: plan the premise, outline and characters, then draft, rewrite and edit over many prompts to keep the plot coherent.

children.name: AgentWrite (plan-then-write long output)
children.desc: Plan paragraphs with a target word count each, then write them in sequence, to get outputs of 10,000+ words.

children.name: RecurrentGPT
children.desc: Imitate an RNN in language: each step writes a paragraph and updates short- and long-term text memories.

children.name: STORM
children.desc: Research-then-write for long articles: find perspectives, simulate expert Q&A grounded in search, outline, then write with citations.

children.name: Chain of Density
children.desc: Iteratively rewrite a summary to pack in more entities at the same length.

children.name: Recursive summarization
children.desc: Summarise chunks, then summarise the summaries, for very long texts.

children.name: Refine summarization
children.desc: Update a running summary chunk by chunk.

children.name: Query-focused summarization
children.desc: Summarise only what bears on a given question or audience.

children.name: Extract-then-abstract
children.desc: Pull the key sentences or facts first, then write the summary from them.

children.name: Key-points and action items
children.desc: Fixed headings for the output, such as decisions, owners and deadlines.

children.name: Summary Chain-of-Thought (SumCoT)
children.desc: First extract the core elements (entity, date, event, result), then write a summary that covers them.

children.name: Code
children.desc: Code prompts work best with executable feedback: tests, error messages and the real context of the repository.

children.name: Spec-first prompting
children.desc: Write a precise specification (inputs, outputs, edge cases) before asking for code.

children.name: Test-driven prompting
children.desc: Supply or have the model write tests first, then code until they pass.

children.name: Signature or interface first
children.desc: Give the function signatures and types, and let the model fill in the bodies.

children.name: Structured CoT (SCoT)
children.desc: Plan the code with sequence, branch and loop structures before writing it.

children.name: Pseudocode first
children.desc: Write pseudocode, then translate it into real code.

children.name: Draft, Sketch, and Prove
children.desc: Write an informal proof, turn it into a formal sketch (Isabelle or Lean), and let automated provers fill the gaps.

children.name: Parsel
children.desc: Break a program down into a hierarchy of functions described in natural language, implement each, and test the combinations.

children.name: Repository context injection
children.desc: Include the relevant files, conventions and the dependency versions in use.

children.name: Explore → plan → code → commit
children.desc: The agent reads the code, writes a plan for approval, implements it, then commits.

children.name: Diff-format output
children.desc: Ask for unified diffs or search-and-replace blocks instead of whole files.

children.name: Style-guide injection
children.desc: Include the linting rules and examples of house style.

children.name: Fill-in-the-middle (FIM)
children.desc: Give the code before and after a gap with sentinel tokens, and the model writes the missing middle.
children.origin: Bavarian et al., 2022; Fried et al., 2022

children.name: Self-debugging
children.desc: The model runs or explains its code, reads the errors and fixes them.

children.name: Error-message feeding
children.desc: Paste the stack trace or failing output back in for a fix.

children.name: Code review prompt
children.desc: Review against a checklist: security, performance, readability, tests.

children.name: Explain-then-fix
children.desc: The model explains what the code does before changing it.

children.name: CodeT (dual execution agreement)
children.desc: Generate code and tests, then pick the code that agrees with the most tests.

children.name: Flow engineering (AlphaCodium)
children.desc: A multi-stage flow: reflect on the problem, generate tests, iterate solutions.

children.name: Multiple solutions plus selection
children.desc: Generate several implementations and choose by tests or a judge.

children.name: Verification by execution
children.desc: Tell the agent to run the tests, the build or a screenshot to verify before reporting done.

children.name: Evolutionary program search (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve)
children.desc: Prompt again and again with the best-scoring programs so far (best-shot prompting); an automatic evaluator scores the new ones.
children.origin: Romera-Paredes et al., 2023; Novikov et al., 2025

children.name: Self-collaboration (role-based coding team)
children.desc: Analyst, coder and tester personas of one model work together on the code.

children.name: Text-to-SQL schema representation
children.desc: Put the database schema (CREATE TABLE statements, foreign keys, sample rows) in the prompt in a format the model handles well.
children.origin: Rajkumar et al., 2022; Gao et al., 2023 (DAIL-SQL)

children.name: DIN-SQL
children.desc: Decomposed text-to-SQL: schema linking, then complexity classification, then SQL generation, then self-correction.

children.name: Multilingual
children.desc: Models often reason best in English, so many multilingual techniques choose which language to think in and which to answer in.

children.name: Translate-first (translate-test)
children.desc: Translate the input into English, solve the task, and translate back if needed.

children.name: Cross-Lingual Thought (XLT)
children.desc: A template that has the model restate the problem in English, reason, then answer in the target language.

children.name: Cross-Lingual Self-Consistency (CLSP)
children.desc: Reason in several languages and vote.

children.name: English instructions, target-language output
children.desc: Keep the instructions in English but name the output language explicitly.

children.name: In-CLT (cross-lingual transfer prompting)
children.desc: Demonstrations that mix source and target languages in the question and answer parts.

children.name: Native-language exemplars
children.desc: Few-shot examples written in the task language.

children.name: PARC
children.desc: Retrieve high-resource-language examples to prompt for a low-resource language.

children.name: X-InSTA
children.desc: Cross-lingual ICL with semantically aligned source-language exemplars and task-based label alignment.

children.name: Dictionary-based prompting (DiPMT)
children.desc: Add dictionary definitions of rare words to translation prompts.

children.name: Chain-of-Dictionary
children.desc: Chain multilingual dictionary entries for rare words in translation.

children.name: MAPS
children.desc: Extract keywords, topics and similar examples before translating.

children.name: Translate-then-refine
children.desc: Draft a translation, then have the model post-edit it.

children.name: Interactive-Chain-Prompting (ICP)
children.desc: Resolve ambiguities before translating by generating clarifying sub-questions and answering them.

children.name: DecoMT
children.desc: Split the source into chunks, translate each with few-shot prompts, then combine them with context in later passes.

children.name: Cultural localisation context
children.desc: Give the locale, audience and cultural norms, not only the language.

children.name: Script and transliteration control
children.desc: Name the script and the romanisation system for the output.

children.name: Multimodal
children.desc: Image, audio and video models have their own prompt grammars, and vision-language models gain from visual markers and describe-first steps.

children.name: Descriptive image prompts
children.desc: Subject, action, setting, medium, style, lighting, lens and composition, in that order.

children.name: Style and quality modifiers
children.desc: Words such as "oil painting", "35mm photo" or "highly detailed" to steer aesthetics.

children.name: Negative prompts
children.desc: List what must not appear: "blurry, extra fingers, text".

children.name: Prompt weighting
children.desc: Raise or lower the weight of terms with syntax such as (term:1.3) or ::2.

children.name: Parameter flags
children.desc: Aspect ratio, seed, stylisation and chaos flags, such as --ar 16:9.

children.name: Prompt rewriting for image models
children.desc: An LLM expands a short idea into a detailed image prompt.

children.name: Image-to-prompt (reverse prompting)
children.desc: Have a model describe an existing image as a generation prompt, then reuse or edit that prompt to reproduce or vary it.

children.name: Quoted text rendering
children.desc: Put any words that must appear in the image inside quotation marks, and say where and in what typeface they go.

children.name: Image prompts (img2img)
children.desc: Give a reference image as a base, with a strength setting.

children.name: Style and character references
children.desc: Reference images that keep a style or a character consistent across generations.

children.name: Inpainting and outpainting prompts
children.desc: Describe only the masked region, or the area to extend.

children.name: Prompt editing (Prompt-to-Prompt)
children.desc: Change one word of the prompt and keep the rest of the image fixed.

children.name: Instruction-based image editing
children.desc: Edit an image with an instruction ("make it winter") instead of re-describing the whole scene.

children.name: Structural conditioning (ControlNet)
children.desc: Condition generation on pose, depth, edge or segmentation maps for precise control of layout.

children.name: Learned concept tokens (Textual Inversion, DreamBooth)
children.desc: Bind a subject or style to a pseudo-word or trigger token, then use it in later prompts.
children.origin: Gal et al., 2022; Ruiz et al., 2022

children.name: Regional prompting
children.desc: Give different sub-prompts to different regions of the canvas, so multi-subject images are composed correctly.

children.name: Prompt scheduling and blending
children.desc: Switch or alternate prompts at set denoising steps, such as [from:to:step] or [a|b], to blend concepts.

children.name: Multimodal CoT
children.desc: First generate a rationale from the image and text, then the answer.

children.name: Duty-Distinct CoT (DDCoT)
children.desc: Split the reasoning into sub-questions, sending the visual ones to a vision model.

children.name: Chain-of-Images
children.desc: Generate intermediate images as reasoning steps.

children.name: Describe-then-answer
children.desc: Ask for a detailed description of the image before the question.

children.name: Multimodal Graph-of-Thought
children.desc: Graph-structured thoughts built from text and image features, instead of linear CoT.

children.name: Socratic Models
children.desc: Combine vision, audio and language models zero-shot by having them exchange natural-language descriptions.

children.name: Visual programming (VisProg, ViperGPT)
children.desc: The model writes a program that calls vision modules (detection, cropping, VQA) to answer a visual question.

children.name: Visual Sketchpad
children.desc: The model draws auxiliary lines, boxes or plots on the image as intermediate reasoning steps.

children.name: Set-of-Mark prompting
children.desc: Overlay numbered marks on image regions so the model can refer to them.

children.name: Visual prompting with boxes, points and arrows
children.desc: Draw on the image to point attention, as also used by segmentation models.

children.name: Image-before-text placement
children.desc: Put images before the question in the prompt.

children.name: Crop and zoom prompting
children.desc: Send crops or tiles of high-resolution images for detail.

children.name: Paired-image (few-shot visual) prompting
children.desc: Before/after or input/output image pairs as demonstrations.

children.name: CLIP prompt templates and ensembling
children.desc: Zero-shot image classification with templates like "a photo of a {label}", averaged across many templates.

children.name: Text-prompted detection and segmentation
children.desc: Use a noun phrase or an exemplar image to find and segment every instance of a concept.
children.origin: Liu et al., 2023 (Grounding DINO); Carion et al., 2025 (SAM 3)

children.name: Grounded coordinate outputs
children.desc: Ask a vision-language model for bounding boxes, points or masks in a set, normalised coordinate format.

children.name: Video prompts
children.desc: Describe shots, camera movement, timing and transitions, often as a storyboard.

children.name: Video-of-Thought
children.desc: Step-by-step video reasoning, from pixel-level grounding of the target to cognitive-level interpretation.

children.name: View-dependent prompting (text-to-3D)
children.desc: Add "front view", "side view" or "back view" for each camera angle during score distillation.

children.name: Keyframe conditioning for video
children.desc: Fix the first frame, or the first and last frames, with images, and use the text prompt only for the motion between them.

children.name: Speech and TTS style prompts
children.desc: Natural-language voice direction or SSML for pace, emotion and emphasis.

children.name: Music prompts
children.desc: Genre, tempo, instruments, mood and structure tags such as [verse] and [chorus].

children.name: Audio and video understanding prompts
children.desc: Ask for timestamps, speaker labels and segment-level answers.

children.name: ASR context prompts
children.desc: Give a speech recogniser a text prompt with the spellings, jargon or punctuation style you want in the transcript.

children.name: Acoustic (reference-audio) prompting
children.desc: Condition speech generation on a short audio clip to copy its voice, prosody or acoustic setting.

children.name: Quality, optimisation & safety
children.desc: Judging outputs, optimising prompts automatically, defending against attacks and tuning the levers around the prompt.

children.name: Evaluation & judges
children.desc: Grading prompts are prompts too: rubrics, reasoning before the score, and bias controls make them reliable.

children.name: LLM-as-a-judge (pointwise)
children.desc: Score one output against criteria.

children.name: Pairwise comparison
children.desc: "Which of A and B is better, and why?"

children.name: Listwise ranking
children.desc: Rank many candidates in one prompt.

children.name: Pairwise Ranking Prompting (PRP)
children.desc: Rank documents by asking the model which of two is more relevant, aggregated by sorting or sliding windows.

children.name: Agent-as-a-Judge
children.desc: An evaluator agent with tools inspects another agent's trajectory and outputs against the requirements, not only the final answer.

children.name: Rubric-based grading
children.desc: Explicit criteria and a description of each score level.

children.name: Reference-guided grading
children.desc: Give a gold answer to compare against.

children.name: G-Eval
children.desc: Auto-generated evaluation steps, form-filling, and a score weighted by token probabilities.

children.name: Explain-then-score
children.desc: The judge writes its critique before the number.

children.name: Binary pass/fail criteria
children.desc: Break quality into yes/no checks, which are more reliable than 1–10 scales.

children.name: Checklist evaluation
children.desc: Generate an instruction-specific checklist and grade each item.

children.name: Anchored scales with examples
children.desc: Show example outputs for each score level.

children.name: Solve-first before grading
children.desc: The judge works out its own solution before evaluating the candidate's answer.

children.name: Position-swap debiasing
children.desc: Run the pairwise judgment in both orders and keep only consistent verdicts.

children.name: Judge calibration against humans
children.desc: Tune the judge prompt until it agrees with human labels.

children.name: Contextual calibration
children.desc: Estimate the model's bias with a content-free input ("N/A") and correct the output probabilities.

children.name: Prompt-format sensitivity testing (FormatSpread)
children.desc: Measure how scores vary across equivalent prompt formats, and report the spread rather than one number.

children.name: Panel of judges (PoLL)
children.desc: Average several smaller judge models to reduce bias.

children.name: Multi-agent evaluation (ChatEval)
children.desc: Judge agents debate before giving a verdict.

children.name: Role-based (multi-persona) evaluation
children.desc: One judge scores from several generated evaluator personas, and the scores are combined.

children.name: Atomic-fact verification (FActScore, SAFE)
children.desc: Split a long answer into atomic facts and check each against a knowledge source or search.
children.origin: Min et al., 2023; Wei et al., 2024

children.name: QA-based faithfulness evaluation (QAGS, FEQA)
children.desc: Generate questions from the output, answer them from both the source and the output, and score how well they agree.
children.origin: Wang et al., 2020; Durmus et al., 2020

children.name: Synthetic test-case generation
children.desc: Have the model write varied and adversarial test inputs for your prompt.

children.name: Golden-dataset regression
children.desc: Re-run a fixed eval set whenever the prompt changes.

children.name: Code-based (deterministic) graders
children.desc: Grade outputs with exact match, regex, JSON-schema checks, numeric tolerance or unit tests, before or instead of an LLM judge.

children.name: Error analysis (trace review and failure taxonomy)
children.desc: Read real traces, label the failures, group them into failure modes, then write targeted evaluators and prompt fixes for the most common ones.

children.name: Prompt optimisation
children.desc: The model can write, score and improve prompts itself, which turns prompt engineering into a search problem.

children.name: Meta-prompting (prompt generator)
children.desc: Ask a model to write or improve the prompt for a task.

children.name: Meta-prompting (conductor)
children.desc: One model acts as a conductor that coordinates expert instances of itself.

children.name: Instruction induction
children.desc: Infer the instruction from input–output pairs.

children.name: PE2
children.desc: A meta-prompt with detailed descriptions and context specification for prompt engineering.

children.name: Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE)
children.desc: Generate candidate instructions from examples, score them and keep the best.

children.name: OPRO
children.desc: The LLM is the optimiser: a meta-prompt holds past prompts and their scores and asks for better ones.

children.name: ProTeGi / APO (textual gradients)
children.desc: Criticise errors in natural language, then edit the prompt using beam search.

children.name: TextGrad
children.desc: Backpropagate textual feedback through multi-step LLM systems.

children.name: PromptAgent
children.desc: Strategic planning (MCTS) over prompt edits from expert-level error reflection.

children.name: GrIPS
children.desc: Gradient-free, edit-based search over instructions.

children.name: GEPA (reflective prompt evolution)
children.desc: Reflect in natural language on execution traces and evolve prompts, with Pareto-based selection of candidates.

children.name: PromptBreeder
children.desc: Self-referential evolution of task prompts and the mutation prompts.

children.name: EvoPrompt
children.desc: Genetic algorithms or differential evolution over prompts.

children.name: RLPrompt
children.desc: Reinforcement learning to optimise discrete prompt tokens.

children.name: AutoPrompt
children.desc: Gradient-guided search for trigger tokens.

children.name: DP2O
children.desc: Policy-gradient RL over a set of prompts generated through multi-turn dialogue with a model.

children.name: DSPy compilation
children.desc: Declare signatures and modules, and let optimisers such as MIPRO tune the instructions and demonstrations.
children.origin: Khattab et al., 2023; Opsahl-Ong et al., 2024

children.name: SAMMO
children.desc: Structure-aware, multi-objective optimisation of prompt programs.

children.name: Prompt compression (LLMLingua)
children.desc: Drop low-information tokens to shorten prompts with little quality loss.

children.name: Prompt A/B testing with evals
children.desc: Compare prompt variants on a test set using metrics or judges.

children.name: Prompt versioning
children.desc: Track prompt changes like code, with diffs and rollback.

children.name: Model-migration rewriting
children.desc: Have the new model rewrite an old prompt for its own quirks.

children.name: Security
children.full: 17. Security: attacks to recognise and defensive prompting
children.desc: Attack families are named here only so you can recognise and defend against them; the defences are the techniques to apply.

children.name: Direct prompt injection
children.desc: User input that tries to override the system instructions.

children.name: Indirect prompt injection
children.desc: Instructions hidden in retrieved web pages, emails, files or tool outputs.

children.name: Prompt leaking
children.desc: Attempts to make the model reveal its system prompt.

children.name: Tool poisoning
children.desc: Malicious instructions hidden in tool or MCP server descriptions, which the model reads as trusted.

children.name: Language model inversion
children.desc: Rebuilding a hidden prompt from the model's outputs or next-token probabilities.

children.name: Jailbreaking (role-play, obfuscation, many-shot)
children.desc: Framings designed to get around safety training.
children.origin: Wei et al., 2023; Anil et al., 2024

children.name: Adversarial suffixes (GCG)
children.desc: Optimised gibberish token suffixes that carry jailbreaks across models.

children.name: Multi-turn escalation (Crescendo)
children.desc: Harmless-seeming conversations that escalate step by step toward a prohibited output.

children.name: Automated attacker-LLM jailbreaks (PAIR, TAP)
children.desc: An attacker model rewrites prompts again and again from the target's responses. Also used for red-teaming.
children.origin: Chao et al., 2023; Mehrotra et al., 2023

children.name: Instruction hierarchy
children.desc: Train or instruct the model to rank system over developer over user over tool content.

children.name: Spotlighting (delimiting, datamarking, encoding)
children.desc: Mark untrusted text so the model treats it as data, never as instructions.

children.name: Sandwich defence
children.desc: Restate the instructions after the untrusted input.

children.name: Random-sequence enclosure
children.desc: Wrap untrusted input in unguessable random delimiters.

children.name: Post-prompting
children.desc: Put the user input before the instructions.

children.name: Self-reminder
children.desc: A system-level reminder to respond responsibly, wrapped around the query.

children.name: In-context defence
children.desc: Demonstrations of refusing harmful requests.

children.name: Instruction defence
children.desc: Warn the model that users may try to change its instructions, and tell it to keep to the task anyway.

children.name: Guard-model screening
children.desc: A separate classifier prompt or model checks inputs and outputs.

children.name: Paraphrase and retokenisation defence
children.desc: Rewrite the input to break adversarial strings.

children.name: Perplexity filtering
children.desc: Reject inputs with abnormal perplexity (gibberish suffixes).

children.name: Canary tokens
children.desc: Plant a secret string to detect prompt leakage.

children.name: Output validation
children.desc: Check outputs against schemas, allow-lists or policies before acting on them.

children.name: Input filtering (block-lists, allow-lists)
children.desc: Screen input for banned words, phrases or patterns before it reaches the model.

children.name: Known-answer detection
children.desc: Ask a detector to repeat a secret key while ignoring the data; if it fails, the data contains an injection.

children.name: SmoothLLM
children.desc: Randomly perturb several copies of the input and combine the responses, to defeat adversarial suffixes.

children.name: Programmable guardrails (NeMo Guardrails)
children.desc: Declarative dialogue rails define allowed topics and flows, and the input and output are checked against them.

children.name: Dual-LLM pattern
children.desc: A privileged LLM never sees untrusted content; a quarantined LLM handles it as symbols.

children.name: CaMeL
children.desc: Separate control flow from data flow, with capability tracking.

children.name: Least-privilege tool scoping
children.desc: Give agents only the tools and permissions the task needs.

children.name: Action-selector pattern
children.desc: The agent only picks from a fixed set of actions, and tool outputs never come back into its context.

children.name: Context-minimization pattern
children.desc: Remove the user's original prompt and other untrusted text from the context before later steps.

children.name: Lethal trifecta / Agents Rule of Two
children.desc: Never let one agent session combine untrusted input, access to sensitive data, and the ability to act or communicate externally.

children.name: Decoding & tuning
children.full: 19. Adjacent levers: decoding, soft prompts and the fine-tuning boundary
children.desc: These are not wording techniques, but prompt engineers tune them together with the prompt, so a complete toolkit includes them.

children.name: Temperature
children.desc: Lower values give more deterministic output; higher values more diverse output.

children.name: Top-p (nucleus) and top-k sampling
children.desc: Cut off the tail of the token distribution.
children.origin: Holtzman et al., 2019; Fan et al., 2018

children.name: Min-p sampling
children.desc: A truncation threshold that scales with the top token's probability.

children.name: Frequency and presence penalties
children.desc: Discourage repeated tokens or topics.

children.name: Logit bias
children.desc: Push specific tokens up or down, or ban them.

children.name: Max tokens
children.desc: A hard cap on output length.

children.name: Seed
children.desc: Reproducible sampling for testing.

children.name: Verbosity parameter
children.desc: An API control over how long and detailed the final answer is, separate from reasoning effort.

children.name: Locally typical sampling
children.desc: Sample tokens whose information content is close to the expected entropy, as an alternative to top-p truncation.

children.name: Logprob inspection
children.desc: Read token probabilities to measure confidence or classify.

children.name: n / best-of sampling
children.desc: Draw several completions per call, for voting or judging.

children.name: Contrastive decoding
children.desc: Choose the tokens the large model prefers much more than a small "amateur" model, to reduce bland or repetitive text.

children.name: CoT-decoding
children.desc: Branch on the top-k first tokens and keep the path with the highest answer confidence, which brings out CoT without any CoT prompt.

children.name: Beam search
children.desc: Deterministic decoding that keeps the top-B partial sequences at each step.

children.name: Classifier-free guidance (CFG)
children.desc: Push the output toward the prompt and away from an unconditional or negative prompt by a set strength. Used in image models and LLMs.

children.name: DoLa (decoding by contrasting layers)
children.desc: Contrast the logits of later and earlier layers during decoding to bring out factual knowledge and reduce hallucination.

children.name: Reasoning effort / thinking budget
children.desc: An API setting for how much the model thinks.

children.name: Prompt caching
children.desc: Reuse a stable prompt prefix to cut cost and latency; put static content first.

children.name: Model selection and cascades
children.desc: Send easy queries to small models and escalate hard ones.

children.name: Budget forcing
children.desc: Control how long the model reasons: append "Wait" to make it keep thinking, or force the end-of-thinking delimiter to stop it.

children.name: Soft prompts (prompt tuning)
children.desc: Learned continuous embeddings prepended to the input.

children.name: Prefix tuning
children.desc: Learned vectors at every layer.

children.name: P-tuning
children.desc: Learned prompt embeddings produced by a small encoder.

children.name: Activation steering
children.desc: Add steering vectors to hidden states. This controls behaviour without any prompt text.

children.name: Graph prompting (GraphPrompt)
children.desc: Learnable task prompts that steer pre-trained graph neural networks. This is the graph-model counterpart of soft prompts.

children.name: Fine-tuning vs prompting decision
children.desc: Move to fine-tuning when prompts become too long, too brittle or too costly.

children.name: Context distillation
children.desc: Fine-tune on outputs produced with a long prompt, so the model behaves that way without the prompt.
children.origin: Askell et al., 2021; Snell et al., 2022
